description: ADJ-LADDER rung 72 — obstetrics amniotic-fluid index from four stated quantities (a NEW panel: obstetrics / amniotic-fluid). From a pocket depth, a transducer factor to divide by, a quadrant gain to scale by, and a probe offset to subtract, compute the amniotic index (pocket_depth/transducer_factor*quadrant_gain-probe_offset), the depth ratio (pocket_depth/transducer_factor), or the scaled pocket (pocket_depth/transducer_factor*quadrant_gain). Each item is a compute_dimensioned program (observe the four quantities, let answer = formula); the ADJ engine carries the arithmetic — a NEW shape, QUOTIENT-TIMES-FACTOR MINUS A TERM a/b*c-d (DIVIDE first, then scale, then subtract — contrast rung-71 a/b*c+d which adds the term, and rung-70 a*b/c-d which multiplies first; the left-to-right a/b*c = a*c/b, not a/(b*c)) — and the harness matches the scalar to the printed options. Contamination-safe: every index is built only from the four observed quantities via /, *, and - — no constant leaks, and neither the depth ratio, the scaled pocket, nor any amniotic figure ever appears as a literal (each is computed) — and the observed quantities carry digit-free identifiers so no numeral hides inside a variable name. The five options are a family over the same four quantities, so the distractors are exactly the slips students make: DIVIDING by the PRODUCT (a/(b*c)-d, a wrong scaling) and SWAPPING the multiply and divide (a*b/c-d, a wrong scaling). The core confusion tested is that a/b*c-d is not a/(b*c)-d and not a*b/c-d.

items.stem: A sonographer records a pocket depth of 24, normalised by a transducer factor of 4, scaled by a quadrant gain of 3 and offset by a probe baseline of 1. What is the corrected amniotic-fluid index (pocket depth normalised, gain-scaled, then offset)?
items.program:
observe pocket_depth(24)
observe transducer_factor(4)
observe quadrant_gain(3)
observe probe_offset(1)
let answer = pocket_depth / transducer_factor * quadrant_gain - probe_offset
? answer

items.stem: A sonographer records a pocket depth of 24, normalised by a transducer factor of 4, scaled by a quadrant gain of 3 and offset by a probe baseline of 1. What is the the depth ratio (pocket depth over the transducer factor)?
items.program:
observe pocket_depth(24)
observe transducer_factor(4)
observe quadrant_gain(3)
observe probe_offset(1)
let answer = pocket_depth / transducer_factor
? answer

items.stem: A sonographer records a pocket depth of 24, normalised by a transducer factor of 4, scaled by a quadrant gain of 3 and offset by a probe baseline of 1. What is the the scaled pocket before subtracting the probe offset (depth ratio times the quadrant gain)?
items.program:
observe pocket_depth(24)
observe transducer_factor(4)
observe quadrant_gain(3)
observe probe_offset(1)
let answer = pocket_depth / transducer_factor * quadrant_gain
? answer
